subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: generates the quantum states (qubits) that carry the key.
parts: attenuated laser (weak coherent pulses) or single-photon source

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: transmits qubits from sender to receiver.
parts: trusted nodes or repeaters for long distance

subsystems.name: Classical channel
subsystems.role: carries basis reconciliation, error correction and authentication messages.
parts: authenticated classical link (e.g., over the internet)

subsystems.name: Post-processing unit
subsystems.role: turns raw detections into a secure key.

subsystems.name: Key management system
subsystems.role: stores and delivers keys to encrypting devices.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the quantum states
buildSteps.detail: A laser and modulators encode random bits into photon polarisation, phase or time-bin, then attenuate the light to single-photon level.

buildSteps.title: Transmit over the quantum channel
buildSteps.detail: Photons travel through optical fibre or free space; losses and noise limit the distance over which keys can be exchanged.

buildSteps.title: Detect and measure
buildSteps.detail: The receiver randomly chooses a measurement basis and records detections, noting the basis and arrival time.

buildSteps.title: Sift the raw key
buildSteps.detail: Over the classical channel, sender and receiver compare bases and keep only the events where they matched.

buildSteps.title: Correct errors
buildSteps.detail: An error-correction protocol reconciles remaining differences, at the cost of leaking some information.

buildSteps.title: Amplify privacy
buildSteps.detail: A hash function compresses the key to remove any information an eavesdropper might have gathered.

buildSteps.title: Authenticate the classical channel
buildSteps.detail: Pre-shared keys or post-quantum signatures prevent a man-in-the-middle attack on the public discussion.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryption
buildSteps.detail: The resulting key is fed to a one-time pad or symmetric cipher for secure communication.

buildSteps.title: Scale the network
buildSteps.detail: Trusted nodes or satellites extend range today; quantum repeaters would remove the need for trusted relays.

prerequisites.why: high-efficiency, low-noise detectors exist but are specialised and costly, limiting key rates and distance.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical fibre or free-space links
prerequisites.why: telecom fibre is widespread, but signal loss still limits practical key exchange to hundreds of kilometres without relays.
they would extend range without trusted nodes by entangling distant qubits, but remain laboratory research.
the classical channel must be authenticated; post-quantum signatures can do this but are not yet widely deployed.
interfaces between QKD hardware and encryption systems are emerging but not yet universal.

pathway.milestone: metro and inter-city QKD links, often using trusted nodes, in finance, government and critical infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: quantum-safe key distribution for high-value fixed links.

pathway.milestone: integration with post-quantum cryptography for authentication and hybrid key exchange; satellite QKD for intercontinental links
pathway.unlocks: wider deployment and resistance to both quantum and classical attacks.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters demonstrated in the lab and early field trials
pathway.unlocks: longer distances without trusted nodes, and the basis of a quantum internet.

pathway.milestone: device-independent QKD and end nodes that are quantum processors
pathway.unlocks: provably secure communication and distributed quantum computing.
